text: In quantitative terms, one can hypothesize a statistical relationship between age at marriage (duration of the learning process) and the literacy rate (as the indicator of development); this is the hypothesis already put forward by Pierre Chaunu in several of his books on European development.’ Indeed, for the whole range of 57 Third World states that provide sound quantitative data - among them the great majority of the Latin American, the Muslim and the Asian countries — the coefficient of correlation between age of women at marriage and global literacy rate (1970-80, all ages) is very high, equalling +0.824 The regions of the world where most of the people can read and write are those where women are not getting married too young, and where the period allotted to the learning process is a long one.

matrilinearity.
